items.title: Cedar Walton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: But that music and the sound of that music is like, just indelible.

Right. Yeah, I was very happy with that 'cause all of a sudden I'll be riding around Manhattan at night in whatever car I was in, on the radio come Mosaic. The guy, uh, Symphony Sid, the DJ, I guess you would call 'em now – we called 'em that then, a Disc Jockey. He would say, "Yes, that was Mosaic composed by See-Dar Walton. He would pronounce it like "radar." [laughs] I always found that amusing but very exhilarating, you know, ridin' around Manhattan hearing your name on the radio with this music. So that was…
In your, generally in your repertoire, you play so many standards …
